stories.title: From Reform to Ruin: the Northern Song Court
stories.blurb: Seventy years of argument over how to govern: Wang Anshi's New Policies, Sima Guang's counter-reform, a cycle of purges, Huizong's splendid court, and the Jurchen sieges that ended the Northern Song.

steps.name: The Myriad Word Memorial
steps.what: Wang Anshi sent Renzong a long memorial calling for reform of government and of the training of officials.
steps.why: It set out the programme he would carry out a decade later.

steps.name: The New Policies begin
steps.what: Shenzong made Wang Anshi assistant councillor, created a Finance Planning Commission and issued the Green Sprouts loan law.
steps.why: The young emperor wanted money and soldiers to face the Liao and Western Xia, and the reforms split the bureaucracy into factions.

steps.name: Sima Guang withdraws to Luoyang
steps.what: The leading critic of the reforms left court and settled in Luoyang to write history.
steps.why: Luoyang became the centre of the opposition while Kaifeng belonged to the reformers.

steps.name: Drought and the refugee picture
steps.what: During a severe drought a gate official sent Shenzong a drawing of starving refugees, blaming the New Policies.
steps.why: The pressure led to Wang Anshi's first resignation.

steps.name: Crow Terrace Poetry Trial
steps.what: Su Shi was jailed and tried for poems said to slander the government, then exiled to Huangzhou.
steps.why: Factional conflict now reached into literature, and dozens of his friends were punished.

steps.name: Zizhi Tongjian presented
steps.what: Sima Guang presented his chronicle of 1,362 years of history to the throne.
steps.why: The work offered rulers lessons from the past and showed the opposition's idea of good government.

steps.name: Shenzong dies, the regency begins
steps.what: Shenzong died and his mother ruled for the eight-year-old Zhezong.
steps.why: The regent recalled the conservatives and turned the government around.

steps.name: The Yuanyou repeal
steps.what: As chief councillor Sima Guang abolished most of the New Policies before dying in office that autumn.
steps.why: Reform and counter-reform became a cycle that each side would repeat.

steps.name: The Shaosheng restoration
steps.what: Ruling in his own right, Zhezong restored the reforms and exiled the Yuanyou officials.
steps.why: The New Policies returned, but now as a weapon in factional revenge.

steps.name: The blacklist stele
steps.what: Cai Jing had the names of Yuanyou officials carved in stone and their families barred from office.
steps.why: Factional purges reached their height and the political class was hollowed out.

steps.name: Alliance Conducted at Sea
steps.what: The Song agreed with the Jurchen Jin to destroy the Liao together.
steps.why: Song military weakness was exposed in the campaign, inviting the Jin to turn south.

steps.name: Abdication and the first siege
steps.what: Huizong abdicated, Li Gang held the walls, and students led by Chen Dong protested at the palace gate until the Jin withdrew for an indemnity.
steps.why: The capital survived once, but the court failed to prepare for the Jin's return.

steps.name: Fall of Kaifeng and the Jingkang incident
steps.what: The Jin took the city, plundered it, set up a puppet ruler, and marched both emperors and the imperial clan north.
steps.why: The Northern Song ended and north China passed to the Jin.

steps.name: A new emperor at Yingtian
steps.what: Prince Kang, the one son of Huizong still free, was enthroned at the Southern Capital.
steps.why: The dynasty survived and soon moved south, beginning the Southern Song.

stories.title: City on the Bian: Money, Craft and Ideas in Song Kaifeng
stories.blurb: How the world's largest city lived: grain fleets on the Bian canal, examinations and academies, floods on the Yellow River, state pharmacies and paper money, clock towers and building manuals, and the paintings that recorded it all before the Jurchen carried its treasures away.

steps.name: The great examination of 1057
steps.what: Ouyang Xiu's examination passed a remarkable group of future writers and philosophers.
steps.why: The examination system drew talent from all over the empire into the capital.

steps.name: New Book of Tang
steps.what: The rewritten official history of the Tang was presented to the throne.
steps.why: Song scholars used the past to argue about moral government in the present.

steps.name: Early Spring
steps.what: The court painter Guo Xi painted his great landscape of a mountain in spring mist.
steps.why: Monumental landscape became the signature art of the Northern Song court.

steps.name: Levelling the Bian canal
steps.what: Shen Kuo measured the fall of the Bian canal using a chain of dykes.
steps.why: The canal carried the grain that fed the capital, and Yellow River silt constantly threatened it.

steps.name: The state goes into trade
steps.what: The State Trade law set up a market bureau in Kaifeng to buy goods and lend to small merchants.
steps.why: The reformers tried to use the capital's commerce to fund the state and curb big dealers.

steps.name: The Yellow River reaches Xuzhou
steps.what: After a breach in Chanzhou, floodwaters surrounded Xuzhou and Su Shi led the work to save the city.
steps.why: The shifting Yellow River was the great hazard of the Song heartland.

steps.name: Coal for the iron works
steps.what: Coal was found near Xuzhou and used to smelt iron, which Su Shi celebrated in verse.
steps.why: Coal and iron were part of the Song's early industrial growth.

steps.name: Clear water for the Bian
steps.what: Water from the Luo River was led into the Bian canal to cut down Yellow River silt.
steps.why: Keeping the grain route open was a constant engineering struggle.

steps.name: Su Song's clock tower
steps.what: A water-driven astronomical clock tower was built in the palace.
steps.why: It was among the most advanced machines of its time.

steps.name: Yingzao Fashi printed
steps.what: The state building manual was printed for use across the empire.
steps.why: Printing spread standard technical knowledge as well as classics.

steps.name: Paper money renamed and overissued
steps.what: The court renamed its paper notes qianyin and extended them, but printed too many.
steps.why: The Song were pioneers of state paper money and of its inflation.

steps.date_note: Approximate; described in a memoir of the city
steps.name: Market days at Xiangguo Temple
steps.what: The great monastery's courtyards filled with traders selling animals, household goods, books and antiques several days each month.
steps.why: Commerce had spread through the whole city, even into its temples.

steps.name: Along the River During the Qingming Festival
steps.what: Zhang Zeduan painted the crowded life of boats, bridges and shops along the Bian.
steps.why: It is the most vivid record of everyday life in a Song city.
steps.wikipedia: Along the River During the Qingming Festival

steps.name: The treasures carried north
steps.what: The Jin took the capital's books, printing blocks, instruments and craftsmen north with the captive emperors.
steps.why: The city's century as the centre of Chinese economy and culture ended.
